annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol version tag for JSON-RPC itself (2.0) — fixed, not MCP-specific.
annotations.id: Client-chosen correlation id (1). The matching response echoes it back so the client can pair request<->response on a single shared stdio pipe.
annotations.method: 'initialize' — the first call of every MCP session. Nothing else may be sent before this completes.
annotations.params.protocolVersion: The MCP spec date-version the client speaks. Server checks this against its own supported versions.
annotations.params.capabilities: Empty here — client is declaring it offers none of the optional client-side features (sampling, roots, elicitation).
annotations.params.clientInfo: Free-text identification of the calling application, for the server's logs — not used for auth.

annotations.id: Echoes 1 — this is the response to the initialize request above.
annotations.result.protocolVersion: The version the SERVER settled on (must match or be acceptable to the client).
annotations.result.capabilities: What the server actually offers: tools (yes, listChanged=false = it won't notify on tool-list changes), resources/prompts (declared but empty — this server exposes neither).
annotations.result.serverInfo: Server's self-reported name ('claims-system' — matches the FastMCP('claims-system') constructor call) and version (the mcp SDK's own version, 1.30.0, not an app version).

annotations.method: 'notifications/initialized' — a NOTIFICATION (no 'id' field), meaning no response is expected or sent. It tells the server the client has finished processing the initialize result and normal requests (tools/list, tools/call, ...) may now begin.

annotations.id: 2 — a fresh id for this request, independent of the initialize exchange.
annotations.method: 'tools/list' — discovery. This is the ONLY thing that produced the tool schemas the model was given; nothing about these two tools is hard-coded in the host.
annotations.params: Empty object — no pagination cursor supplied, so the server returns its full tool list in one page.

exchange.raw:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[{"name":"get_claim_status","description":"Look up the current status of a claim by claim number.

Args:
    claim_number: e.g. "CLM-2024-88120".

Returns:
    status, policy_id, claimant_name, opened_date, last_updated.
","inputSchema":{"properties":{"claim_number":{"title":"Claim Number","type":"string"}},"required":["claim_number"],"title":"get_claim_statusArguments","type":"object"}},{"name":"get_adjuster_notes","description":"Return the adjuster note history for a claim, oldest first.

Args:
    claim_number: e.g. "CLM-2024-88120".

Returns:
    claim_number and a chronological list of {date, author, note}.
","inputSchema":{"properties":{"claim_number":{"title":"Claim Number","type":"string"}},"required":["claim_number"],"title":"get_adjuster_notesArguments","type":"object"}}]}}

tools.name: get_claim_status
tools.description:
Look up the current status of a claim by claim number.

Args:
    claim_number: e.g. "CLM-2024-88120".

Returns:
    status, policy_id, claimant_name, opened_date, last_updated.

tools.name: get_adjuster_notes
tools.description:
Return the adjuster note history for a claim, oldest first.

Args:
    claim_number: e.g. "CLM-2024-88120".

Returns:
    claim_number and a chronological list of {date, author, note}.

annotations.result.tools: Array of Tool objects. Each one's 'name' and 'description' come verbatim from the Python function name and docstring in claims_system_server.py (get_claim_status, get_adjuster_notes) — FastMCP generated this JSON from the decorated functions, nothing here was hand-written as JSON.
annotations.result.tools[].inputSchema: JSON Schema auto-derived from the Python function's type-hinted parameters (claim_number: str -> {'type':'string'}), with 'required' populated from parameters that have no default.

annotations.id: 3 — a fresh id for this call.
annotations.method: 'tools/call' — an actual invocation, distinct from tools/list (listing a tool never runs it).
annotations.params.name: Which discovered tool to run — must be one of the names tools/list just returned.
annotations.params.arguments: The call's arguments, validated by the server against that tool's inputSchema before the Python function runs.

annotations.result.content: MCP wraps every tool's return value as a list of content blocks (here one 'text' block) rather than returning arbitrary JSON directly — this is what lets a tool return images/embedded resources too, not just text. The text itself is this server's get_claim_status() return value, JSON-serialized by FastMCP.
annotations.result.isError: false — a normal, successful result. Had the Python function raised instead, this would be true and 'content' would carry the exception's str() as the recoverable error message (see error_before_after.md for that path in the OTHER server).

model_call_location: Where the model call happens and where it does not, in one line: every message in this file is client<->server tool plumbing that never touches an LLM; the ONE place an LLM is called in this whole system is week9_mcp/host/agent.py's _call_model() (Groq chat.completions.create), which runs in the HOST process after tools/list has already returned — this server only ever sees initialize/tools/list/tools/call and has no model client, API key, or prompt anywhere in it.
